clue.text: Red Lane? Go use a posh alternative!

definitions.note: 'red lane' is old nursery slang for the throat, the passage food goes down

indicators.note: an alternative version of these words is a fresh arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that a street name sounds common, with a grander replacement urged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges the ten letters of GO USE A POSH; 'Red Lane' is a childish name for the gullet, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lane is the throat, and the food pipe running down from it is the gullet.

clue.text: Response from city and half of Soho

parts.note: EC is the postal district of the City of London

indicators.note: half of the word Soho, here its back half

explanation.surface: Reaction from the City and part of Soho, two London districts.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London; EC is the postcode of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated back, a reply.

clue.text: Nothing survives of the oil producers

parts.note: O, like zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody is left alive among the oil companies.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of the olive tree is pressed for its oil.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

explanation.surface: A prisoner with an identifying tag hidden in hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A captive held to force others to meet demands.

explanation.surface: A plant's shoot starts to increase in size.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to shoot up like a plant, and to get bigger is to increase in size.

clue.text: Being unproductive tires out the French

indicators.note: out implies the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Laziness exhausts the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren, giving no yield or offspring.

parts.note: a colour applied at the tips of the hand, its extremities, not a useful shade

explanation.surface: A very useful paint colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel applied to fingertips, at the very ends of the hand.

clue.text: A number of horses, about ten, can be exacting

parts.note: a string is the group of racehorses kept by one stable

indicators.note: about suggests the word ten is moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing stable of around ten animals proves demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEN into ENT; 'can be' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent can mean severe or harsh, as of stern criticism.

explanation.surface: Someone makes it past a barrier because they hold a ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through an exam is to succeed in it, and a free admission ticket or permit is also called this.

clue.text: Common donkey has fetters in front-dangerous way to draw

indicators.note: says the fetters come before the donkey in the answer

parts.note: fetters are chains for the legs
moke is a common, slangy British word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A donkey wearing leg irons up front, like a hazardous way to pull a cart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like pulling a load or sketching, but here it means drawing on a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting one cigarette from another means drawing on tobacco without a break, a habit that is a health hazard.

clue.text: Wave or means to make one?

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of curl a hairdresser might produce, and with what.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on the first: a hair curler is the tool for putting a wave in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A long breaking ocean wave is so called, and so is a curler used to set waves in hair.

clue.text: Bulletin muddle takes a long time

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A confused news bulletin that drags on for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official communication or notice.

clue.text: Foot-long skeleton from Sumatra set out

indicators.note: out implies these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A long skeleton found on Sumatra and put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones running the length of the foot between the ankle and toes form part of the skeleton.

parts.note: the substance used to make impressions on posted letters, not an art movement's medium

explanation.surface: What painters after Impressionism worked with.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax used to seal envelopes, pressed with a signet that leaves an impression.

explanation.surface: A gallant exclamation urging people forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word as EARL plus -LY, in the manner of a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming before the expected time, and read as an adverb from a peer's title it means aristocratically.

clue.text: Company for philosopher having no retirement

indicators.note: retirement is a withdrawal or going back, so the word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: Asking whether a philosopher will keep company and never retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' turns NO into ON after PLATO.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a military unit, a subdivision of an army company.

parts.note: plum means choice or first-rate, as in a plum job
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A quality pen with a fine nib.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather, whose quill was once a writing pen.

clue.text: Good score from non-U league, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as a possible rearrangement once the U is dropped

explanation.surface: A fine result in a football league outside the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' says take U out of LEAGUE; 'perhaps' rearranges the remaining LEAGE. 'Non-U' is also British slang for not upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, two strokes under par on a hole is a very good score.

explanation.surface: A cheeky complaint about a small reduction in rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky drop' is a drop running down the cheek; 'rent' is the noun for a rip, not the payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of liquid from the eye rolls down the cheek, and a rent in cloth is a rip.

indicators.note: put out suggests the word fire is disturbed and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Fires are often extinguished, a common occurrence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread or prevalent is common.

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a sump is the reservoir of an engine where oil drains

explanation.surface: An engine's oil collecting at the bottom, left in the drain.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic depression is a slump in trade.

explanation.surface: Complaining about the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh criticism, and covering a roof with tiles of slate.

explanation.surface: Which neckwear suits an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow' is the front of a boat: the rope tied there for mooring is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: A mooring rope fixed at a boat's bow, and a person who makes pictures with brush and pigment.

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible rearrangement of the given letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a writer's prose is literary or merely dull.
explanation.walkthrough: LITTERY is not a word; it is simply fodder that 'possibly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian means dull and unoriginal, so done in a stale, hackneyed manner.

parts.note: the range in which sounds reach our ears, read as a definition rather than a report of overhearing

explanation.surface: A remark about the space where we can catch sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the distance over which sound can be heard by a listener.

explanation.surface: Plates stacked in layers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat thin layers, and thin flat pieces of metal or glass.

clue.text: Stew for those in a bad temper?

explanation.surface: A stew served to diners who are grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: To lose one's rag is British slang for losing one's temper; someone with the rag out is read as RAG OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragout is a highly seasoned meat stew; having one's rag out suggests an angry mood.

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the abbreviation
back means the word nip is read backwards

explanation.surface: Popping out again after a second drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A short ride in a car for pleasure.

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac is a casual name for a Scotsman; the other sense is an old tax, as in scot-free.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Scotland, and an old word for a payment or levy, surviving in 'scot-free'.

clue.text: Replacing piece in mat and showing intolerance

indicators.note: replacing the letters puts them back in a new order

explanation.surface: A repair to a mat that shows somebody lost patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance of delay or annoyance is an inability to wait calmly.

clue.text: State of university head reversing headgear

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
reversing means the word for headgear is read backwards

explanation.surface: A college principal turning their cap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the United States, in the west of the country.

clue.text: Charity in which energy is to be controlled

indicators.note: something controlled is reined in and organised afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A charity whose drive must be channelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in the sense of kindness and willingness to give freely.
